passages.text: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Put your house in order, for you are about to die; you will not recover.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah became very sick.
Hezekiah’s sickness was so serious that he was about to die.
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah was the son of Amoz.
Isaiah came to Hezekiah.
Isaiah spoke to Hezekiah.
Isaiah said, “This is what the LORD says.”
Isaiah said, “Put your house in order.”
Isaiah said, “You are going to die.”
Isaiah said, “You will not recover.”
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לָמ֑וּת וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵ֠לָיו יְשַׁעְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־ אָמ֜וֹץ הַנָּבִ֗יא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ צַ֣ו לְבֵיתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י מֵ֥ת אַתָּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִֽחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD, saying, “Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what was good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah became very sick.
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
Hezekiah said, “Please, O LORD, remember me.
I have walked before You faithfully.
I have served You with a whole heart.
I have done what is good in Your sight.”
Hezekiah wept with great sorrow.
passages.original: וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת־ פָּנָ֖יו אֶל־ הַקִּ֑יר וַיִּ֨תְפַּלֵּ֔ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ אָנָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה זְכָר־ נָ֞א אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנֶ֗יךָ בֶּֽאֱמֶת֙ וּבְלֵבָ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם וְהַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עָשִׂ֑יתִי וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל׃ס

passages.text: Before Isaiah had left the middle courtyard, the word of the LORD came to him, saying, “Go back and tell Hezekiah the leader of My people that this is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: ‘I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. I will surely heal you. On the third day from now you will go up to the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
He was the son of Amoz.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah was very sick and near death.
Isaiah had not yet left the middle courtyard.
The word of the LORD came to Isaiah.
The LORD spoke to Isaiah.
The LORD told Isaiah to return to Hezekiah.
The LORD called Hezekiah the leader of His people.
The LORD is the God of David, Hezekiah’s ancestor.
The LORD said, “I have heard your prayer.”
The LORD said, “I have seen your tears.”
The LORD said, “I will heal you.”
The LORD said, “On the third day from now, you will go up to the house of the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ לֹ֣א יָצָ֔א הָעִיר הַתִּֽיכֹנָ֑ה וּדְבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה הָיָ֥ה אֵלָ֖יו לֵאמֹֽר׃ שׁ֣וּב וְאָמַרְתָּ֞ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ נְגִיד־ עַמִּ֗י כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔יךָ שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־ תְּפִלָּתֶ֔ךָ רָאִ֖יתִי אֶת־ דִּמְעָתֶ֑ךָ הִנְנִי֙ רֹ֣פֶא לָ֔ךְ בַּיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י תַּעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: I will add fifteen years to your life. And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city for My sake and for the sake of My servant David.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Hezekiah through Isaiah.
God promised to add fifteen years to Hezekiah’s life.
God said He would rescue Hezekiah from the king of Assyria.
God said He would also rescue the city from the king of Assyria.
God promised to defend the city.
God said He would do this for His own sake.
God said He would also do this for the sake of His servant David.
passages.original: וְהֹסַפְתִּ֣י עַל־ יָמֶ֗יךָ חֲמֵ֤שׁ עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּמִכַּ֤ף מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁוּר֙ אַצִּ֣ילְךָ֔ וְאֵ֖ת הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וְגַנּוֹתִי֙ עַל־ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃

passages.text: Then Isaiah said, “Prepare a poultice of figs.” So they brought it and applied it to the boil, and Hezekiah recovered.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
He spoke to the people of Israel.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah was sick.
Isaiah said, “Prepare a poultice of figs.”
The people brought the figs.
They made a poultice.
They put the poultice on Hezekiah’s boil.
Hezekiah recovered.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ קְח֖וּ דְּבֶ֣לֶת תְּאֵנִ֑ים וַיִּקְח֛וּ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ עַֽל־ הַשְּׁחִ֖ין וַיֶּֽחִי׃

passages.text: Now Hezekiah had asked Isaiah, “What will be the sign that the LORD will heal me and that I will go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah spoke to Isaiah.
Hezekiah asked Isaiah a question.
Hezekiah said, “What sign will the LORD give me?”
Hezekiah wanted to know if the LORD would heal him.
Hezekiah also wanted to know if he would go up to the house of the LORD on the third day.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶֽל־ יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ מָ֣ה א֔וֹת כִּֽי־ יִרְפָּ֥א יְהוָ֖ה לִ֑י וְעָלִ֛יתִי בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And Isaiah had replied, “This will be a sign to you from the LORD that He will do what He has promised: Would you like the shadow to go forward ten steps, or back ten steps?”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
Isaiah spoke to Hezekiah.
Isaiah said, “This is a sign for you from the LORD.
The LORD will do what He has promised.
You will see a sign.
The shadow can go forward ten steps.
Or the shadow can go back ten steps.
Which do you choose?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֗הוּ זֶה־ לְּךָ֤ הָאוֹת֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֚י יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר הָלַ֤ךְ הַצֵּל֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר מַֽעֲל֔וֹת אִם־ יָשׁ֖וּב עֶ֥שֶׂר מַעֲלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: “It is easy for the shadow to lengthen ten steps,” answered Hezekiah, “but not for it to go back ten steps.”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah spoke to Isaiah.
Hezekiah said, “It is easy for the shadow to go forward ten steps.
But it is not easy for the shadow to go back ten steps.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ נָקֵ֣ל לַצֵּ֔ל לִנְט֖וֹת עֶ֣שֶׂר מַעֲל֑וֹת לֹ֣א כִ֔י יָשׁ֥וּב הַצֵּ֛ל אֲחֹרַנִּ֖ית עֶ֥שֶׂר מַעֲלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: So Isaiah the prophet called out to the LORD, and He brought the shadow back the ten steps it had descended on the stairway of Ahaz.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah called out to the LORD.
The LORD answered Isaiah.
The LORD moved the shadow back.
The shadow had gone down ten steps on the stairway of Ahaz.
The LORD brought the shadow back up those ten steps.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֛א יְשַׁעְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֶת־ הַצֵּ֗ל בַּֽ֠מַּעֲלוֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרְדָ֜ה בְּמַעֲל֥וֹת אָחָ֛ז אֲחֹֽרַנִּ֖ית עֶ֥שֶׂר מַעֲלֽוֹת׃פ

passages.text: At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard about Hezekiah’s illness.
passages.sermon:
Merodach-baladan was the son of Baladan.
Merodach-baladan was the king of Babylon.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah became ill.
Merodach-baladan heard that Hezekiah was ill.
At that time, Merodach-baladan sent letters to Hezekiah.
He also sent a gift to Hezekiah.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֡יא שָׁלַ֡ח בְּרֹאדַ֣ךְ בַּ֠לְאֲדָן בֶּֽן־ בַּלְאֲדָ֧ן מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֛ל סְפָרִ֥ים וּמִנְחָ֖ה אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י חָלָ֖ה חִזְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: And Hezekiah received the envoys and showed them all that was in his treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, as well as his armory—all that was found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his palace or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah received the envoys from Babylon.
Hezekiah showed the envoys everything in his treasure house.
He showed them the silver.
He showed them the gold.
He showed them the spices.
He showed them the precious oil.
He showed them his armory.
He showed them all that was found in his storehouses.
Hezekiah did not hide anything from the envoys.
He showed them everything in his palace.
He showed them everything in all his dominion.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע עֲלֵיהֶם֮ חִזְקִיָּהוּ֒ וַיַּרְאֵ֣ם אֶת־ כָּל־ בֵּ֣ית נְכֹתֹ֡ה אֶת־ הַכֶּסֶף֩ וְאֶת־ הַזָּהָ֨ב וְאֶת־ הַבְּשָׂמִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת׀ שֶׁ֣מֶן הַטּ֗וֹב וְאֵת֙ בֵּ֣ית כֵּלָ֔יו וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִמְצָ֖א בְּאֽוֹצְרֹתָ֑יו לֹֽא־ הָיָ֣ה דָבָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־ הֶרְאָ֧ם חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּבֵית֖וֹ וּבְכָל־ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the prophet Isaiah went to King Hezekiah and asked, “Where did those men come from, and what did they say to you?” “They came from a distant land,” Hezekiah replied, “from Babylon.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
He went to King Hezekiah.
Isaiah spoke to Hezekiah.
Isaiah asked, “What did those men say?”
Isaiah also asked, “Where did they come from?”
Hezekiah answered Isaiah.
Hezekiah said, “They came from a distant land.”
Hezekiah said, “They came from Babylon.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו מָ֥ה אָמְר֣וּ׀ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וּמֵאַ֙יִן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ מֵאֶ֧רֶץ רְחוֹקָ֛ה בָּ֖אוּ מִבָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: “What have they seen in your palace?” Isaiah asked. “They have seen everything in my palace,” answered Hezekiah. “There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
He spoke to King Hezekiah.
Isaiah asked Hezekiah a question.
He said, “What did the men see in your palace?”
Hezekiah answered Isaiah.
He said, “They saw everything in my palace.”
Hezekiah said, “There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֥ה רָא֖וּ בְּבֵיתֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ אֵ֣ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּבֵיתִי֙ רָא֔וּ לֹא־ הָיָ֥ה דָבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ הִרְאִיתִ֖ם בְּאֹצְרֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD: The time will surely come when everything in your palace and all that your fathers have stored up until this day will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
He spoke to King Hezekiah.
Isaiah said, “Hear the word of the LORD.”
The LORD says this:
A time is coming.
Everything in your palace will be taken away.
All the treasures your fathers stored up until today will be taken away.
They will be carried off to Babylon.
Nothing will remain.
The LORD has spoken this.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר־ יְהוָֽה׃ הִנֵּה֮ יָמִ֣ים בָּאִים֒ וְנִשָּׂ֣א׀ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵיתֶ֗ךָ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר אָצְר֧וּ אֲבֹתֶ֛יךָ עַד־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה בָּבֶ֑לָה לֹֽא־ יִוָּתֵ֥ר דָּבָ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah spoke to Hezekiah.
Isaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Isaiah said that some of Hezekiah’s descendants will be taken away.
These descendants will be Hezekiah’s own children and grandchildren.
They will be taken from their homeland.
They will become eunuchs.
They will serve in the palace of the king of Babylon.
passages.original: וּמִבָּנֶ֜יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵצְא֧וּ מִמְּךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תּוֹלִ֖יד יִקָּח וְהָיוּ֙ סָֽרִיסִ֔ים בְּהֵיכַ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: But Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good.” For he thought, “Will there not at least be peace and security in my lifetime?”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Isaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Isaiah spoke a message from the LORD to Hezekiah.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good."
Hezekiah thought about his own life.
Hezekiah said, "Will there not be peace and truth in my days?"
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶֽל־ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ ט֥וֹב דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֲל֛וֹא אִם־ שָׁל֥וֹם וֶאֱמֶ֖ת יִהְיֶ֥ה בְיָמָֽי׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, along with all his might and how he constructed the pool and the tunnel to bring water into the city, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was a king of Judah.
Hezekiah did many things.
Hezekiah showed great strength.
Hezekiah built a pool.
Hezekiah made a tunnel.
Hezekiah brought water into the city.
The Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah records these things.
passages.original: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ וְכָל־ גְּב֣וּרָת֔וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה אֶת־ הַבְּרֵכָה֙ וְאֶת־ הַתְּעָלָ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת־ הַמַּ֖יִם הָעִ֑ירָה הֲלֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: And Hezekiah rested with his fathers, and his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah died.
Hezekiah was buried with his ancestors.
Manasseh was Hezekiah’s son.
Manasseh became king after Hezekiah died.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
